replies.text:
Two different scenarios. WA is FAR from socialist. It's had a historically very regressive tax structure. Also, you wanna talk "socialism", let's talk about Massachusetts. WA has no state income tax. MA does. The San Juan County population is relatively old: 38.6% of residents were 65 or older in the 2020–2024 Census estimates.  All five places have affordability problems, while the San Juan Islands have a particularly pronounced year-round economic sustainability problem. The difference is between two kinds of expensive island living: Expensive but relatively affluent: Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard have very high property values, wealthy second-home owners, and substantial tourism economies. Expensive relative to the local economy: The San Juan Islands have high housing and operating costs, but a much smaller local employment and income base. San Juan County has a comparatively low-wage economy. Its housing market is influenced by wealthy second-home buyers and people bringing income from elsewhere. Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket have larger tourism economies and more developed institutional infrastructure. They also have substantial wealth, philanthropy, nonprofit housing organizations, and employer-supported housing programs, you know "socialism". For example, a 2026 Nantucket employer survey found that 68% of responding employers provided some form of housing support.  The San Juans have fewer resources to absorb the economic consequences of expensive housing and labor shortages. 

Also, tho eastern lslands are also distressed, so lets not ignore that.

comments.author: @BrockMcLellan
comments.text:
In 1963, when I was 15 and living in New Westminster, British Columbia, near Vancouver, Canada, I was told that from the next summer I would be expected to work during the summer, so this would be my last family vacation. I was asked where I wanted to go. Without hesitation, I said Orcas Island, which was where my family went. I had already been to most of the Canadian Gulf Islands, such as Galiano, Mayne and Saltspring. Soon after, my parents bought property on Saltspring Island, but decided to sell it and move to Qualicum Beach on Vancouver Island, for their retirement. I think they felt the Gulf Islands were just too isolated.

By 1980, my wife and I had moved to Norway. For the past 38 years, we have lived on a cliff 35 m above sea level, and 50 m from the sea. Our daughter took her secondary education on Vancouver Island, followed by university degrees in Vancouver, and Umeå, Sweden. She decided that both BC and Scandinavia were far too cold for her, so she moved to California. 

There is something about the combination of land and sea that attracts people.

comments.text: I live on Orcas and for about 25 years. I agree with most of what is said on this video. You are either grandfathered in due to your family that got in early when it was affordable or you have to be part of a program like Opal, or in my case a program where you have to build your home, "sweat equity". The issue with vacation homes is that it's a double edged sword. On the one hand it's what fuels the economy here but then on the other hand it's what keeps people from being able to afford a home out here. There has been a lot of recent low income type housing but it only allows you to own the home not the land. Add fuel is way higher than anywhere else. Often $1.50 higher. Food is also expensive requiring a trip off island to Costco which is a all day trip and an expensive boat ride. And I agree with one commenter that wages are the lowest when you account for the cost of living. After 25 years I'm looking to move. Not because of the cost but because of the isolation. It's pretty but you are subjected to the same narrow paths you are allowed to travel so you see the exact same scenery which is beautiful but the same. You can't do anything spontaneous unless it's on the island. You can't leave without careful planning. Want to see a concert off island? Prepare to get a hotel room. And if you are off just for a day you have to plan part of your time around the ferry. You have to be there early both ways which makes for a long day much of which has nothing to do with why you are off to begin with. It's definitely a love hate relationship.
